text: If $\int \frac{\sin ^{\dfrac{3}{2}}x+\cos ^{\dfrac{3}{2}}x}{\sqrt{\sin ^{3}x\cos ^{3}x\sin (x-θ)}}dx=A\sqrt{\cos θ\tan x-\sin θ}+B\sqrt{\cos θ-\sin θ\cot x}+C$, where $C$ is the integration constant, then $AB$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \int \dfrac{\sin ^{\frac{3}{2}}x+\cos ^{\frac{3}{2}}x}{\sqrt{\sin ^{3}x\cos ^{3}x\sin (x-θ)}}dx \\ I=\int \dfrac{\sin ^{\frac{3}{2}}x+\cos ^{\frac{3}{2}}x}{\sqrt{\sin ^{3}x\cos ^{3}x(\sin x\cos θ-\cos x\sin θ)}}dx \\ =\int \dfrac{\sin ^{\frac{3}{2}}x}{\sin ^{\frac{3}{2}}x\cos ^{2}x\sqrt{\tan x\cos θ-\sin θ}}dx+\int \dfrac{\cos ^{\frac{3}{2}}x}{\sin ^{2}x\cos ^{\frac{3}{2}}x\sqrt{\cos θ-\cot x\sin θ}}dx= \\ \int \dfrac{\sec ^{2}x}{\sqrt{\tan x\cos θ-\sin θ}}dx+\int \dfrac{\mathrm{cosec}^{2}x}{\sqrt{\cos θ-\cot x\sin θ}}dx \\  \end{array}$

$\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_{1}+\mathrm{I}_{2}$ ...... {Let}

For $\mathrm{I}_{1}$, let $\tan \mathrm{x}\cos θ-\sin θ=\mathrm{t}^{2}$

$\sec ^{2}xdx=\frac{2tdt}{\cos θ}$

For $\mathrm{I}_{2}$, let $\cos θ-\cot \mathrm{x}\sin θ=\mathrm{z}^{2}$

$\mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx=\frac{2zdz}{\sin θ}$

$\begin{array}{l} I=I_{1}+I_{2} \\ =\int \dfrac{2tdt}{\cos θt}+\int \dfrac{2zdz}{\sin θz} \\ =\dfrac{2t}{\cos θ}+\dfrac{2z}{\sin θ} \\ =2\sec θ\sqrt{\tan x\cos θ-\sin θ}+2\mathrm{cosec}θ\sqrt{\cos θ-\cot x\sin θ} \\ \text{Comparing} \\ AB=8\mathrm{cosec}2θ \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: The distance of the point $(2,3)$ from the line $2x-3y+28=0$, measured parallel to the line $\sqrt{3}x-y+1=0$, is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
The line $\sqrt{3}x-y+1=0$ has slope $\sqrt{3}$, so the distance is measured along the direction $θ=60^{\circ }$. The point at distance $r$ from $A(2,3)$ in this direction is

$P\left (2+\dfrac{r}{2},3+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}r}{2}\right )$

$P$ lies on $2x-3y+28=0$:

$2\left (2+\dfrac{r}{2}\right )-3\left (3+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}r}{2}\right )+28=0\Rightarrow 23=r\left (\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}-1\right )$

$r=\dfrac{46}{3\sqrt{3}-2}=\dfrac{46\left (3\sqrt{3}+2\right )}{27-4}=2\left (3\sqrt{3}+2\right )=4+6\sqrt{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: Let a unit vector $\hat{u}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ make angles $\frac{π}{2},\frac{π}{3}$ and $\frac{2π}{3}$ with the vectors $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{k},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{k}$ and $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}$ respectively. If $⃗{v}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{k}$ then $|\hat{u}-⃗{v}|^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Unit vector $\hat{\mathrm{u}}=\mathrm{x}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{y}\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\mathrm{z}\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \vec{\mathrm{p}}_{1}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{k}},\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ \vec{\mathrm{p}}_{3}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{j}} \end{array}$

Now angle between $\hat{\mathrm{u}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{1}=\frac{π}{2}$

$\hat{\mathrm{u}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{p}}_{1}=0\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{x}}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\mathrm{z}}{\sqrt{2}}=0$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{z}=0$ ...... (i)

Angle between $\hat{\mathrm{u}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{2}=\frac{π}{3}$

$\hat{\mathrm{u}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{p}}_{2}=|\hat{\mathrm{u}}|\cdot \left |\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{2}\right |\cos \frac{π}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{z}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow y+z=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ ...... (ii)

Angle between $\hat{\mathrm{u}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{3}=\frac{2π}{3}$

$\hat{\mathrm{u}}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{p}}_{3}=|\hat{\mathrm{u}}|\cdot \left |\vec{\mathrm{p}}_{3}\right |\cos \frac{2π}{3}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{y}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{-1}{2}\Rightarrow x+y=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}$ ..... (iii)

from equation (i), (ii) and (iii) we get

$x=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}y=0z=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Thus}\hat{\mathrm{u}}-\vec{\mathrm{v}}=\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{k}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ \hat{\mathrm{u}}-\vec{\mathrm{v}}=\dfrac{-2}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ \therefore |\hat{\mathrm{u}}-\vec{\mathrm{v}}|^{2}=\left (\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{5}{2} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: If R is the smallest equivalence relation on the set $\{1,2,3,4\}$ such that $\{(1,2),(1,3)\}\subset \mathrm{R}$, then the number of elements in $\mathrm{R}$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An equivalence relation containing $(1,2)$ and $(1,3)$ must contain $(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4)$ by reflexivity and $(2,1),(3,1)$ by symmetry.

By transitivity, $(2,1)$ and $(1,3)$ force $(2,3)$, and then symmetry forces $(3,2)$. So $1,2,3$ form one equivalence class.

Nothing requires $4$ to be related to another element, so the smallest such relation has classes $\{1,2,3\}$ and $\{4\}$:

$R=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4),(1,2),(2,1),(1,3),(3,1),(2,3),(3,2)\},$

which has $3^{2}+1=10$ elements.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: If the mean and variance of five observations are $\frac{24}{5}$ and $\frac{194}{25}$ respectively and the mean of the first four observations is $\frac{7}{2}$, then the variance of the first four observations is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The five observations have mean $\dfrac{24}{5}$, so $x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}+x_{5}=24$; the first four have mean $\dfrac{7}{2}$, so $x_{1}+x_{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}=14$ and $x_{5}=10$.

From the variance of all five observations:

$\dfrac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{5}x_{i}^{2}}{5}-\left (\dfrac{24}{5}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{194}{25}\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{5}x_{i}^{2}=5\times \dfrac{194+576}{25}=154$

Removing $x_{5}^{2}=100$ gives $x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+x_{3}^{2}+x_{4}^{2}=154-100=54$.

Variance of the first four observations:

$\dfrac{54}{4}-\left (\dfrac{7}{2}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{54}{4}-\dfrac{49}{4}=\dfrac{5}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: If $\sin \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )=\log _{e}|x|+\frac{α}{2}$ is the solution of the differential equation $x\cos \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )\frac{dy}{dx}=y\cos \left (\frac{y}{x}\right )+x$ and $y(1)=\frac{π}{3}$, then $α^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Differential equation :-

$\begin{array}{l} x\cos \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y\cos \dfrac{y}{x}+x \\ \cos \dfrac{y}{x}\left [x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y\right ]=x \end{array}$

Divide both sides by $\mathrm{x}^{2}$

$\cos \frac{y}{x}\left (\frac{x\frac{dy}{dx}-y}{x^{2}}\right )=\frac{1}{x}$

Let $\frac{y}{x}=t$

$\begin{array}{l} \cos \mathrm{t}\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right )=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}} \\ \cos \mathrm{t}\mathrm{dt}=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{dx} \end{array}$

Integrating both sides

$\begin{array}{l} \sin \mathrm{t}=\ln |\mathrm{x}|+\mathrm{c} \\ \sin \dfrac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=\ln |\mathrm{x}|+\mathrm{c} \end{array}$

Using $\mathrm{y}(1)=\frac{π}{3}$, we get $\mathrm{c}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

So, $α=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow α^{2}=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: An integer is chosen at random from the integers $1,2,3,\ldots ,50$. The probability that the chosen integer is a multiple of atleast one of 4, 6 and 7 is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Among $1,2,\ldots ,50$, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be the sets of multiples of 4, 6 and 7 respectively.

$n(A)=⌊\dfrac{50}{4}⌋=12$, $n(B)=⌊\dfrac{50}{6}⌋=8$, $n(C)=⌊\dfrac{50}{7}⌋=7$.

A number is a multiple of both 4 and 6 exactly when it is a multiple of $\text{lcm}(4,6)=12$; these are $12,24,36,48$, so $n(A\cap B)=4$.

Likewise $A\cap C$ holds the multiples of 28 (only 28), $B\cap C$ the multiples of 42 (only 42), and $A\cap B\cap C$ the multiples of 84 (none), so these counts are 1, 1 and 0.

$n(A\cup B\cup C)=12+8+7-4-1-1+0=21$

The required probability is $\dfrac{21}{50}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: If each term of a geometric progression $a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots$ with $a_{1}=\frac{1}{8}$ and $a_{2}\neq a_{1}$, is the arithmetic mean of the next two terms and $S_{n}=a_{1}+a_{2}+\ldots ..+a_{n}$, then $S_{20}-S_{18}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the GP be $ar^{n-1}$. Given,

$\begin{array}{l} 2a_{r}=a_{r+1}+a_{r+2} \\ 2ar^{n-1}=ar^{n}+ar^{n+1} \\ \dfrac{2}{r}=1+r \\ r^{2}+r-2=0 \end{array}$

Hence, we get, $r=-2$ (as $r\neq 1$)

So, $\mathrm{S}_{20}-\mathrm{S}_{18}=$ (Sum upto 20 terms) $-$ (Sum upto 18 terms) $=\mathrm{T}_{19}+\mathrm{T}_{20}$

$\mathrm{T}_{19}+\mathrm{T}_{20}=\mathrm{ar}^{18}(1+\mathrm{r})$

Putting the values $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{8}$ and $\mathrm{r}=-2$;

we get $T_{19}+T_{20}=-2^{15}$

text: Let $\mathrm{r}$ and $θ$ respectively be the modulus and amplitude of the complex number $z=2-i\left (2\tan \frac{5π}{8}\right )$, then $(\mathrm{r},θ)$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\tan \dfrac{5π}{8}=\tan \left (π-\dfrac{3π}{8}\right )=-\tan \dfrac{3π}{8}$,

$z=2-2i\tan \dfrac{5π}{8}=2+2i\tan \dfrac{3π}{8}$

As $0<\dfrac{3π}{8}<\dfrac{π}{2}$, both $\cos \dfrac{3π}{8}$ and $\tan \dfrac{3π}{8}$ are positive, so $z$ lies in the first quadrant.

$z=\dfrac{2}{\cos \frac{3π}{8}}\left (\cos \dfrac{3π}{8}+i\sin \dfrac{3π}{8}\right )=2\sec \dfrac{3π}{8}\left (\cos \dfrac{3π}{8}+i\sin \dfrac{3π}{8}\right )$

With $2\sec \dfrac{3π}{8}>0$, this is the polar form, so $r=2\sec \dfrac{3π}{8}$ and $θ=\dfrac{3π}{8}$.

In (C), $2\sec \dfrac{5π}{8}=-2\sec \dfrac{3π}{8}<0$, so it cannot be a modulus.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The sum of the solutions $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ of the equation $\frac{3\cos 2x+\cos ^{3}2x}{\cos ^{6}x-\sin ^{6}x}=x^{3}-x^{2}+6$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{3\cos 2x+\cos ^{3}2x}{\cos ^{6}x-\sin ^{6}x}=x^{3}-x^{2}+6 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\cos 2x\left (3+\cos ^{2}2x\right )}{\cos 2x\left (1-\sin ^{2}x\cos ^{2}x\right )}=x^{3}-x^{2}+6 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{4\left (3+\cos ^{2}2x\right )}{\left (4-\sin ^{2}2x\right )}=x^{3}-x^{2}+6 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{4\left (3+\cos ^{2}2x\right )}{(3+\cos ^{2}2x)}=x^{3}-x^{2}+6 \\ x^{3}-x^{2}+2=0\Rightarrow (x+1)\left (x^{2}-2x+2\right )=0 \end{array}$

so, sum of real solutions $=-1$

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & 2 & 11 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$ and $P=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 \\ 7 & 1 & 5 \end{array}\right ]$. The sum of the prime factors of $\left |P^{-1}AP-2I\right |$ is equal to

text: Let the set $C=\left \{(x,y)|x^{2}-2^{y}=2023,x,y\in \mathrm{ℕ}\right \}$. Then $\sum\limits _{(x,y)\in C}(x+y)$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, let's consider the equation $x^{2}-2^{y}=2023$ where $x$ and $y$ are natural numbers. Our goal is to find all the pairs $(x,y)$ that satisfy this equation and then sum the values of $x+y$ for each pair in set $C$.

Since $2023$ is an odd number, and $x^{2}$, the square of any natural number, is even when $x$ is even and odd when $x$ is odd, we can determine that for the left-hand side of the equation to be odd (thus equal to $2023$), $x$ must be odd since the right-hand side of the equation ($2^{y}$) is always even as it represents a power of two.

Also, $2023$ can be factored into prime factors to further analyze the possible solutions:

$2023=7\times 17\times 17$

Thus, allowing us to rewrite the equation as:

$x^{2}-2^{y}=7\times 17^{2}$

The next step is to check for potential values of $x$ that would fit the equation, keeping in mind that $x$ must be odd. We can try to express $x^{2}$ as $7\times 17^{2}$ plus a power of $2$, recognizing that we are looking for the decomposition of the form:

$x^{2}=7\times 17^{2}+2^{y}$

By examining the powers of $2$ and keeping in mind that they grow very quickly, we can reason that $y$ cannot be very large because $x^{2}$ must not exceed $2023$ by a large margin.

Let's start by trying the lowest values for $y$ since that would make $2^{y}$ small and $x$ has a better chance of being a natural number:

For $y=1$:

$x^{2}=2023+2^{1}=2023+2=2025$

Surprisingly, we find a perfect square since $45^{2}=2025$. Therefore, $(x,y)=(45,1)$ is one solution.

For $y=2$ or higher:

$2^{y}$ becomes at least $4$ and increases exponentially, so $x^{2}$ must be at least $2027$ or higher in such cases. There's no natural number between $45$ and $46$, and $46^{2}$ far exceeds the target (2116), making it impossible for $x^{2}$ to be less than $2116$ for any larger $y$.

Hence, it appears there is only one possible solution: $(x,y)=(45,1)$.

Therefore, the sum $\sum\limits _{(x,y)\in C}(x+y)$ for this set will consist of only this one pair:

$\sum\limits _{(x,y)\in C}(x+y)=45+1=46$

So the answer is $46$.

text: Let $α,β$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}-\sqrt{6}x+3=0$ such that $\mathrm{Im}(α)>\mathrm{Im}(β)$. Let $a,b$ be integers not divisible by 3 and $n$ be a natural number such that $\frac{α^{99}}{β}+α^{98}=3^{n}(a+ib),i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then $n+a+b$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x^{2}-\sqrt{6}x+3=0$, the discriminant is $6-12=-6$, so

$x=\dfrac{\sqrt{6}\pm i\sqrt{6}}{2}=\sqrt{3}\cdot \dfrac{1\pm i}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{3}e^{\pm iπ/4}$

Since $\mathrm{Im}(α)>\mathrm{Im}(β)$, $α=\sqrt{3}e^{iπ/4}$ and $β=\sqrt{3}e^{-iπ/4}$, so $\dfrac{α}{β}=e^{iπ/2}=i$.

$\dfrac{α^{99}}{β}+α^{98}=α^{98}\left (\dfrac{α}{β}+1\right )=α^{98}(1+i)$

$α^{98}=3^{49}e^{i98π/4}=3^{49}e^{i(24π+π/2)}=3^{49}i$

So the expression equals $3^{49}i(1+i)=3^{49}(-1+i)$.

Comparing with $3^{n}(a+ib)$, where $a$ and $b$ are not divisible by 3, gives $n=49$, $a=-1$, $b=1$, so $n+a+b=49-1+1=49$.

Hence, the answer is 49.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

$\begin{array}{l} x+y+z=6, \\ 2x+5y+αz=β\text{and} \end{array}$

$x+2y+3z=4$, has infinitely many solutions. Then $(PQ)^{2}$ is equal to $_________$.

solution.body:
$\because \mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\mathrm{c}$ are in A.P

$\Rightarrow 2b=a+c\Rightarrow a-2b+c=0$

$\therefore \mathrm{ax}+\mathrm{by}+\mathrm{c}$ passes through fixed point $(1,-2)$

$\therefore \mathrm{P}=(1,-2)$

For infinite solution,

$\begin{array}{lllllll} D=D_{1}=D_{2}=D_{3}=0 \\ D:\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & α \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Rightarrow α=8 \\ D_{1}:\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ β & 5 & α \\ 4 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=0\Rightarrow β=6 \\ \therefore Q=(8,6) \\ \therefore (PQ)^{2}=(8-1)^{2}+(6+2)^{2}=113 \end{array}$

text: Let $P(α,β)$ be a point on the parabola $y^{2}=4x$. If $P$ also lies on the chord of the parabola $x^{2}=8y$ whose mid point is $\left (1,\frac{5}{4}\right )$, then $(α-28)(β-8)$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Parabola is $x^{2}=8y$

Chord with mid point $(\mathrm{x}_{1},\mathrm{y}_{1})$ is $\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{S}_{1}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \mathrm{xx}_{1}-4(\mathrm{y}+\mathrm{y}_{1})=\mathrm{x}_{1}^{2}-8\mathrm{y}_{1} \\ \therefore (\mathrm{x}_{1},\mathrm{y}_{1})=\left (1,\dfrac{5}{4}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}-4\left (\mathrm{y}+\dfrac{5}{4}\right )=1-8\times \dfrac{5}{4}=-9 \end{array}$

$\therefore x-4y+4=0$ ...... (i)

$(α,β)$ lies on (i) & also on $y^{2}=4x$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore α-4β+4=0\text{.... (ii)} \\ &β^{2}=4α\text{.... (iii)} \end{array}$

Solving (ii) & (iii)

$\begin{array}{l} β^{2}=4(4β-4)\Rightarrow β^{2}-16β+16=0 \\ \therefore β=8\pm 4\sqrt{3}\text{and}α=4β-4=28\pm 16\sqrt{3} \\ \therefore (α,β)=(28+16\sqrt{3},8+4\sqrt{3})& \\ (28-16\sqrt{3},8-4\sqrt{3}) \\ \therefore (α-28)(β-8)=(\pm 16\sqrt{3})(\pm 4\sqrt{3}) \\ =192 \end{array}$

text: Let $f(x)=\sqrt{\lim _{r\to x}\left \{\frac{2r^{2}[(f(r))^{2}-f(x)f(r)]}{r^{2}-x^{2}}-r^{3}e^{\frac{f(r)}{r}}\right \}}$ be differentiable in $(-\infty ,0)\cup (0,\infty )$ and $f(1)=1$. Then the value of $ea$, such that $f(a)=0$, is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(1)=1,f(a)=0 \\ f^{2}(x)=\lim _{r\to x}\left (\dfrac{2r^{2}(f^{2}(r)-f(x)f(r))}{r^{2}-x^{2}}-r^{3}e^{\frac{f(r)}{r}}\right ) \\ =\lim _{r\to x}\left (\dfrac{2r^{2}f(r)}{r+x}\dfrac{(f(r)-f(x))}{r-x}-r^{3}e^{\frac{f(r)}{r}}\right ) \\ f^{2}(x)=\dfrac{2x^{2}f(x)}{2x}f^{'}(x)-x^{3}e^{\frac{f(x)}{x}} \\ y^{2}=xy\dfrac{dy}{dx}-x^{3}e^{\frac{y}{x}} \\ \dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{x^{2}}{y}e^{\frac{y}{x}} \end{array}$

Put $y=vx\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$

$\begin{array}{l} v=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}-\dfrac{x}{v}e^{v} \\ \dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{v}}{v}\Rightarrow e^{-v}vdv=dx \end{array}$

Integrating both side

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c})+1+\mathrm{v}=0 \\ \mathrm{f}(1)=1\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=1,\mathrm{y}=1 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow c=-1-\dfrac{2}{e} \\ e^{v}\left (-1-\dfrac{2}{e}+x\right )+1+v=0 \\ e^{\frac{y}{x}}\left (-1-\dfrac{2}{e}+x\right )+1+\dfrac{y}{x}=0 \\ x=a,y=0\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{2}{e} \\ ae=2 \end{array}$

text:
If $\int\limits _{\frac{π}{6}}^{\frac{π}{3}}\sqrt{1-\sin 2x}dx=α+β\sqrt{2}+γ\sqrt{3}$, where $α,β$ and $γ$ are rational numbers, then
$3α+4β-γ$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $1-\sin 2x=(\sin x-\cos x)^{2}$, the integrand is $\sqrt{1-\sin 2x}=|\sin x-\cos x|$.

On $\left [\dfrac{π}{6},\dfrac{π}{4}\right ]$, $\cos x\geq \sin x$, and on $\left [\dfrac{π}{4},\dfrac{π}{3}\right ]$, $\sin x\geq \cos x$, so

$\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/3}\sqrt{1-\sin 2x}dx=\int\limits _{π/6}^{π/4}(\cos x-\sin x)dx+\int\limits _{π/4}^{π/3}(\sin x-\cos x)dx$

The first part is $[\sin x+\cos x]_{π/6}^{π/4}=\sqrt{2}-\dfrac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

The second part is $[-\cos x-\sin x]_{π/4}^{π/3}=\sqrt{2}-\dfrac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

Adding, the integral is $-1+2\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}$, so $α=-1$, $β=2$, $γ=-1$ and

$3α+4β-γ=-3+8+1=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
